analysis:
Both changed files are test scripts (scripts/test-provider-release-pipeline.py, scripts/test-provider-release-resolution.py). No production code, workflow or release logic changes in the supplied evidence, so no runtime attack surface is added.

Pipeline test changes (head lines 367-372, 698-701, 857-859): the warm-cache test now pins a nightly cron, forbids a master branch push trigger and the 'scripts/**' path filter in provider-release-cache.yml, requires cancel-in-progress, and gates warming on needs.gate.outputs.run. These tighten the assertions that warming has no secrets, no contents: write and no release creation (lines 382-384 are unchanged). The cluster-runtime script test (698-701) now checks the caller trigger paths by exact line and checks DEV_CALLER with a looser substring match. That is a weaker assertion, but it only covers path-filter coverage for release triggers, not a credential boundary. The publication requirements pin assertion (857-859) is similarly relaxed for DEV_CALLER.

Resolution test additions (head lines 107-121): they assert that a workflow_dispatch on refs/heads/dev publishes only a dev-branch build. The assertions cover version 0.9.0-dev.branch.42 and publish=true, with the validation and version overrides ignored. Environments other than dev are refused with 'Dev branch releases publish dev only'. This strengthens the guard that a non-tag or branch trigger cannot reach the staging or prod signing identity, which the existing prod-tag-gate test (lines 491-501) also pins. The real behavior lives in scripts/resolve-provider-release.sh and the release-dev-branch.yml caller, neither of which was supplied. I cannot verify that the actual resolver and workflows match these tests, and that is a coverage limit, not a finding.

No threat-model IDs (A-011, T-034, TB-009, and so on) are directly affected by test-only changes. The next pass should verify that resolve-provider-release.sh, release-dev-branch.yml and provider-release-cache.yml implement what the tests now pin.
